content.title: About
content.content: Beans are the seeds of plants in the genus Phaseolus (most often Phaseolus vulgaris) that grow in pods. They are native to the Americas and are now grown all over the world. There are many varieties, including white, red, black, and speckled beans, as well as green beans. Beans have a mild, earthy flavor and a creamy texture when cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The common bean was domesticated in the Americas thousands of years ago.
White, red, black, and speckled beans often belong to the same species, Phaseolus vulgaris.
Green beans are eaten together with their pods, while mature dried beans are eaten only after long cooking.
Beans are a staple of traditional cuisines in Latin America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.
Dried beans can be stored for a very long time, but they take longer to cook as they age.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Beans provide protein and are often used in plant-based diets in place of meat.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and helps you feel full.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is important for cell formation and especially needed when planning a pregnancy.

items.title: Contains iron, magnesium, and potassium
items.content: These minerals support oxygen transport and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Thanks to protein and fiber, the carbohydrates in beans are absorbed more slowly.

items.title: Raw beans are toxic
items.content: Raw or undercooked beans, especially red kidney beans, contain lectins that can cause severe stomach upset.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gas; soaking them and introducing them gradually can help.

items.title: Salt in canned beans
items.content: Canned beans can be high in salt; rinsing them helps.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Beans are legumes, and allergic reactions are possible, including cross-reactions with other legumes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak dried beans for 8–12 hours, drain, and cook until completely soft. Red kidney beans should first be boiled hard for at least 10 minutes and then simmered until tender. Cooked beans can be added to soups, salads, stews, purees, and fillings. Canned beans are best rinsed before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep cooked beans in the refrigerator for 3–5 days or freeze them. Store canned beans in a cool place, and after opening, transfer them to a covered container in the refrigerator.

content.title: About
content.content: Black toasted bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from rye and wheat, often sweetened with caramelized sugar or molasses, which gives it a dark color and a subtle sweet aroma. After baking, the slices are toasted until crisp, enhancing flavor and making them ideal for sandwiches and snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black bread is traditionally considered more nutritious than white bread because it contains more whole grains.
Toasting triggers the Maillard reaction, creating a characteristic caramelized taste.
In countries such as Russia and Poland, black bread is a staple and is frequently served with soups.
The dark color can be achieved by adding molasses or by a longer fermentation of the dough.
Toasted bread is often used as a base for bruschetta – open‑face sandwiches with various toppings.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and bran in black bread provide a high amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Sourdough fermentation preserves B1, B2 and B3 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The loaf supplies iron, magnesium and zinc, which aid immune function and energy production.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Thanks to whole grains and fermentation, black bread promotes satiety and causes a slower rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Caramelized sugars and whole grains contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bread made from wheat and rye contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Some black bread recipes use a notable amount of salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Toasting adds a small amount of fat, so excessive consumption may lead to extra calorie intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted black bread works well for sandwiches with cheese, ham, avocado or pâté. It can also be used for croutons, soup toppings, or as a crunchy side for salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag; thaw and toast before use.

content.title: About
content.content: Turkish coffee is a finely ground coffee brewed in a special pot (cezve) and served in small cups. The preparation involves bringing the mixture to a boil several times, creating a thick foam and a rich aroma. Traditionally it is unfiltered, often sweetened and sometimes flavored with cardamom or other spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkish coffee is one of the oldest coffee preparation methods, with a history of over 500 years.
In Turkey and many Middle Eastern countries coffee is served with a glass of water to cleanse the palate.
The coffee grounds left in the cup are used for fortune‑telling, a practice known as tasseography.
Turkish coffee was inscribed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
Traditional preparation requires slow heating over low heat to avoid over‑boiling.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Improves alertness
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, enhancing concentration and reaction time.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption can boost metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Turkish coffee provides magnesium, potassium and manganese, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Enhances mood
items.content: Caffeine promotes the release of dopamine and serotonin, which can improve mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia or rapid heartbeat after coffee.

items.title: Increased stomach acidity
items.content: Coffee can aggravate gastritis and heartburn in susceptible people.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain medications, such as antidepressants and stimulants.

items.title: Potential risk for pregnant women
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit caffeine intake to about 200 mg per day.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare Turkish coffee in a cezve by adding cold water, finely ground coffee and sugar to taste. Bring the mixture to a boil 2–3 times, then pour into small cups and let the grounds settle. Serve without milk, optionally flavored with cardamom or cinnamon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground Turkish coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. For best flavor use within 2–3 months of grinding. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato, scalloped, NFS (4208) is a ready‑to‑eat product made from selected potatoes sliced thinly and baked in a creamy cheese sauce. It is produced gluten‑free and designed for quick preparation in a microwave or conventional oven.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Scalloped potatoes became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
NFS stands for "No Further Seasoning" – the product is ready to eat without additional seasoning.
One serving provides about 150 kcal, making it a convenient snack.
Cheddar cheese is commonly used, creating a golden crust when baked.
The product is packaged in a sealed film that preserves freshness for up to 12 months.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C contributes to immune support and protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: The product is formulated with minimal added salt, beneficial for blood‑pressure management.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates in potatoes are readily absorbed, providing fast energy.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cheese component may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes can raise blood‑sugar levels quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some versions may contain preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive to food additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the product in a microwave (2–3 minutes) or bake in an oven at 180 °C for 12–15 minutes. Serve as a side dish, a standalone meal, or add to salads. Fresh herbs can be sprinkled on top for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal the package tightly. Shelf life shortens at temperatures above 25 °C.
